title: Rebuilding Community Through Sport: A Commentary on the Role of Pickup Soccer and Basketball in Addressing Loneliness and Isolation
abstract: ABSTRACT Loneliness and social isolation represent a public health crisis with serious consequences for overall well‐being. With access to medical and mental health care in the United States hindered by stigma, cost and time constraints, alternative pathways to holistic wellness are urgently needed. Sports, especially team sports like basketball and soccer, offer an effective way to promote health among youth due to their cultural resonance and accessibility. While the sport for development (SFD) and positive youth development (PYD) literature has well‐documented the individual‐level benefits of sport participation, scholars increasingly call for a shift towards community‐centred theory and practice that extends beyond personal gains. This conceptual paper contributes to that conversation by examining how basketball and soccer can address loneliness and isolation at both the individual and community level with an emphasis on informal play in the form of pickup games. We highlight how these sports foster social connection and buffer against the harmful effects of the current loneliness epidemic. We also offer practical recommendations for stakeholders seeking to integrate basketball and soccer into SFD programming and other recreational spaces. Finally, we conclude with a call to action urging the adoption of a transformative SFD model, one that actively counters loneliness and cultivates meaningful community connections.

journal.name: JOURNAL OF COMMUNITY & APPLIED SOCIAL PSYCHOLOGY
